title: Head-space P4 versus MODFLOW prepared-solve ownership reconciliation

technical_history.mechanism: The first harness divided two near-equal head differences to infer a dimensionless contraction fraction. The ratio accumulated approximately 2.49e-12 absolute floating-point error even though exact sequential factor-1/2 arithmetic reproduced the persisted accepted head bit-for-bit.
technical_history.repair: Use the actual sequential P4 factor-1/2 arithmetic as the gate. No physical, numerical, ownership or compatibility criterion changed.

bounded_conclusions: The frozen G11/G17 P4 recovery genuinely requires two sequential head-space contractions; the first accepted head is reproduced exactly by applying factor 1/2 twice to the raw proposal around the current head.

The current F-GC38 prepared-solve participant exposes response publication and solve progression, but no admitted operation that sets X to an externally prescribed contracted head, restores the previous X, rolls back one external nonlinear iteration, clones an open solve, or restarts the same open solve from XOLD.
F-GC39 explicitly requires continuous MODFLOW X across nonconverged coupling iterations and forbids groundwater rollback/discard between them.
Therefore exact G11/G17 head-space P4 cannot be composed unchanged with the current F-GC38/F-GC39 prepared-solve ownership contract.
This does not invalidate P4 as research evidence and does not invalidate the prepared-solve architecture. It identifies a missing composition bridge.
Direct mutation of the live NumPy X pointer is not an admitted solution because it would bypass the qualified F-GC38 ownership contract.
A response-space globalization rule is a distinct candidate and must be separately derived and qualified rather than relabelled as P4.
next_natural_unit: Derive and qualify a prepared-solve-native response-space damping bridge. First test whether interpolating the affine response intercept reproduces the frozen head-space P4 contractions in the G11 affine-groundwater stress; only then test the rule inside a continuous live F-GC38 prepared solve.
